paper.title: KL-UCB-switch: optimal regret bounds for stochastic bandits from both a distribution-dependent and a distribution-free viewpoints

settings.name_in_paper: Bounded stochastic K-armed bandit over [0,1], known horizon T
settings.definition_quote: We consider the simplest case of a bounded stochastic bandit problem with finitely many arms indexed by $a \in \{1,\ldots,K\}$ and with rewards in~$[0,1]$. ... We first consider a fixed and beforehand-known value of~$T$.

settings.name_in_paper: Bounded stochastic K-armed bandit over [0,1], unknown horizon (anytime)
settings.definition_quote: We consider the simplest case of a bounded stochastic bandit problem with finitely many arms indexed by $a \in \{1,\ldots,K\}$ and with rewards in~$[0,1]$. ... Adaptation to the Horizon $T$ (an Anytime Version of KL-UCB-Switch)

source.label: th:distribfree
source.quote: Given $T \geq 1$, the regret of the KL-UCB-Switch algorithm, tuned with the knowledge of $T$ and the switch function $f(T, K) = \lfloor (T/K)^{1/5} \rfloor$, is uniformly bounded over all bandit problems $\unu$ over $[0,1]$ by R_T \leq (K-1) + 23 \sqrt{KT}.

results.notes: Regret defined as sum_a Delta_a E[N_a(T)] (pseudo-regret). Compute: requires computing Kinf indices; polynomial per round not explicitly stated but implied.

symbols.Kinf_a: K_inf(nu_a, mu_star): infimum of KL(nu_a, nu') over distributions nu' on [0,1] with mean > mu_star
symbols.c_a: O_T(1) term, finite-time closed form given in Eq. (detailedboundTh3)

extra_assumptions: bound per suboptimal arm a on expected number of pulls E[N_a(T)]

source.label: th:distribdependentloglog
source.quote: Given $T \geq 1$, the KL-UCB-Switch algorithm, tuned with the knowledge of $T$ and the switch function $f(T, K) = \lfloor (T/K)^{1/5} \rfloor$, ensures that for all bandit problems $\unu$ over $[0,1]$ with $\mu^\star \in (0,1)$, for all sub-optimal arms~$a$, for all $T \geq K/\min\big\{1-\mu^\star, \,(\Delta_a/9)^{12}\big\}$, \E[N_a(T)] \leq \frac{\ln T - \ln \ln T}{\Kinf(\nu_a, \mu^\star)} + \O_T(1)

results.notes: Quantity is expected number of pulls of a suboptimal arm (regret = sum Delta_a times this). O_T(1) term represented by distribution-dependent constant c_a.

source.label: th:distfreeanytime
source.quote: The regret of the anytime version of KL-UCB-Switch algorithm above, tuned with the switch function $f(t, K) = \lfloor (t/K)^{1/5} \rfloor$, is uniformly bounded over all bandit problems $\unu$ over $[0,1]$ as follows: for all $T \geq 1$, R_T \leq (K-1) + 44 \sqrt{KT}.

bound.regime: for all T >= 1 (second-order term asymptotic in T)

symbols.Kinf_a: K_inf(nu_a, mu_star): infimum of KL(nu_a, nu') over distributions on [0,1] with mean > mu_star
symbols.c_a: distribution-dependent constant in the O_T((ln T)^{6/7}) term; closed form in Eq. (thdistrdep:precisebound:anytime)

extra_assumptions: bound per suboptimal arm a on expected number of pulls E[N_a(T)]

source.label: th:asymptoticanytime
source.quote: The anytime version of KL-UCB-Switch algorithm above, tuned with the switch function $f(t, K) = \lfloor (t/K)^{1/5} \rfloor$, ensures that for all bandit problems $\unu$ over $[0,1]$, for all sub-optimal arms $a$, for all $T \geq 1$, \E[N_a(T)] \leq \frac{\ln T }{\Kinf(\nu_a, \mu^\star)} + \O_T\bigl( (\ln T)^{6/7} \bigr)

results.notes: Quantity is expected pull count of suboptimal arm. O_T term represented as c_a*(ln T)^{6/7}.
